Subject: Three MUST-FAIL vectors for the reporting format

Hi Guigui, the ACB-CG reporting format work is exactly the right step. Here are three MUST-FAIL test vectors from CSOAI's operational 22-axis signed measurement instrument (Ed25519 cards + Merkle root + Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps, 257 leaves live at councilof.ai).

**MUST-FAIL #1: Retroactive anchoring.** Valid Merkle proof included in card, but anchor timestamp is LATER than the claimed measurement time → verification MUST FAIL. Prevents retroactive anchoring of pre-existing measurements, which is the most common integrity bug we've seen in practice.

**MUST-FAIL #2: Signature substitution.** card_id matches the signed payload, but signature key is different from issuer_did → MUST FAIL. Catches card cloning attacks where someone re-signs a real card with their own key.

**MUST-FAIL #3: n-count inflation.** Card lists n_measurements=N, but items.jsonl has fewer rows → MUST FAIL. Catches the failure mode of claiming more measurements than actually exist.

All three vectors are CC0 (public domain) and we provide reference test data at councilof.ai/w3c-must-fail/. Happy to adapt the wording for any reporting format the group converges on.

— Nicholas Templeman, CSOAI Ltd (UK 16939677)
